294	// for the commands that write agent settings, repository files and git hooks (a typo would otherwise
295	// run a setup); their flags are the ones HELP lists plus the few every command takes. The other
296	// commands keep taking any flag.
297	const COMMON_FLAGS = ['repo', 'dry', 'json', 'quiet', 'yes', 'verbose', 'background', 'no-learn', 'serve-only', 'help'];
298	// setup still takes the flags of the cache build it no longer runs (2026-10-21), so an old script does not stop on them
299	const UNLISTED_FLAGS = { setup: ['export', 'build', 'no-build', 'depth', 'agent', 'prs', 'pr', 'no-docs', 'benchmark', 'no-benchmark', 'no-prs', 'slug', 'no-phrase', 'model', 'project', 'directories', 'full-repo', 'areas', 'no-seed'], rewire: ['quiet', 'json'] };
300	const STRICT_COMMANDS = ['setup', 'connect', 'uninstall', 'rewire', 'doctor'];
301	function helpFlags(c, help = HELP) {
302	  const lines = help.split('\n');
303	  const start = lines.findIndex(l => new RegExp(`^  ${c}( |$)`).test(l));
304	  if (start < 0) return null;
305	  const block = [lines[start]];
306	  for (let i = start + 1; i < lines.length && !/^  \S/.test(lines[i]); i++) block.push(lines[i]);
307	  return [...new Set((block.join('\n').match(/--[a-z][a-z-]*/g) || []).map(f => f.slice(2)))];
308	}
309	function unknownFlags(c, given, help = HELP) {
310	  if (!STRICT_COMMANDS.includes(c)) return [];
311	  const known = new Set([...(helpFlags(c, help) || []), ...(UNLISTED_FLAGS[c] || []), ...COMMON_FLAGS]);
312	  return Object.keys(given).filter(f => !known.has(f));
313	}
